Hi all —

Thanks Priya for the clear redlines. I reviewed MedDyne_MSA_redline_v3.docx and flagged three substantive items that need direct discussion:

1) EU carveout: The proposed language currently seeks a cap on liability that excludes GDPR fines. We cannot explicitly accept exclusion of regulatory fines. We can offer: (a) a limitation on liability with carveouts for gross negligence and willful misconduct, and (b) an indemnity approach for third-party data breach claims tied to Redwood's processing — but we need to scope responsibilities in the Data Processing Addendum (DPA).

2) Multi-entity signature: We are comfortable executing the Order Form via Redwood Inference, Inc. for commercial terms; however, if MedDyne requires a specific subsidiary to receive invoices (for tax/regulatory reasons), we need that mapped on the Order Form. Please confirm which MedDyne legal entity will be the contracting counterparty vs. the billing entity.

3) Audit/evidence: The redline asks for 36 months of telemetry retention for audit. Our standard is 24 months; we can extend to 30 months as a one-time concession for enterprise customers, but anything beyond will need a contract-level pricing adjustment.

I'm assigning a couple of inline suggestions in the doc (see tracked changes). Can Priya confirm the contracting vs billing entity and whether MedDyne can accept a 30-month telemetry retention?

If you prefer a quick call for the carveout language I'll be available 1/14 11:00–12:00 PT.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Hi Priya —

I've gone through your OrderForm_PO_schema_v2.xlsx and MedDyne_portal_fields.csv. A few operational notes and action items for the portal team: 

- PO line-level: We support line-item granularity with up to 10 custom attributes per line. For your EDI mapping, column "PO_LINE_FLAG" should map to our internal skuFlag and will determine whether items require manual acknowledgement.
- Invoice encryption: We support SFTP+PGP and an optional HTTPS JSON endpoint with payload-level AES-256 encryption using an exchange key. SFTP+PGP is the easiest for Ariba-style gateways; I'll attach a short spec in this thread (attachment stub).
- Tax/jurisdiction: If MedDyne will remit to a non-US billing entity, we need the billing VAT/Tax ID in the portal registration fields. That is currently a required field for activation.

Deliverables: 
- I'll upload a mapping CSV with the final column names for your Ariba admin by EOD 1/15.
- I'll also include a sample SFTP key exchange guide and PGP pubkey stub.

One technical question for procurement: do you require PON-level electronic acknowledgements routed back to MedDyne's EDI AS2 endpoint, or will email acknowledgements suffice for the pilot? AS2 ack will require additional integration work (estimated 3–5 business days).

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Integration Lead — Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai

Attachment: portal_integration_spec_stub.txt

Thanks team —

Appreciate the quick reviews. Answers below: 
- Contracting vs billing entity: MedDyne, Inc. (US) will be the contracting counterparty. For billing, we may use MedDyne Global Services BV (NL) for EU invoices. I'll confirm legal names and VAT IDs by EOD 1/15.
- Telemetry retention: We can accept 30 months.
- AS2 acknowledgements: For the pilot we will accept email acknowledgements; pilot scope may expand to AS2 for production.

Next asks: 
1) Marissa — once Mateo posts the mapping CSV, can you queue a portal activation slot? We need sandbox provisioning before DocuSign so our EDI team can validate line mapping (target: sandbox by 1/20).
2) Kimberly — once we have final contracting entity and the DPA addendum, can you provide the final tracked MSA by 1/16 so procurement can route internally?

If we can keep to those targets, I think 1/23 remains realistic for sign-off.

Regards,
